newsitem.title: UK: EU 14 refinery runs down one percent in February.
newsitem.headline: EU 14 refinery runs down one percent in February.

text.p: Refinery output in 14 member states of the European Union fell by 1.0 percent or 127,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 11.999 million bpd from January's revised level of 12.126 million bpd, Stichting Euroilstock said in its monthly report published on Monday.
But while output was down from January's level, it was up 2.1 percent or 247,000 bpd from the level last February.

The biggest percentage change was for naphtha, where production rose by 4.3 percent or 42,000 bpd from January's level to 1.021 million bpd. Naphtha output was also 1.9 percent above the February 1996 level, Euroilstock said.
Gasoline production also rose, by 0.7 percent or 21,000 bpd from January to 3.218 bpd. This was 177,000 bpd above the February 1996 level.

Output of other products fell. Middle distillate production, covering gas oil and jet, fell 1.1 percent or 62,000 bpd to 5.519 million bpd, although this was still an increase of 133,000 bpd from last February's level.
And fuel oil production fell by 1.6 percent or 28,000 bpd to 1.691 million bpd. Fuel oil output was also off by 127,000 bpd from last February's production level.

Although refinery runs were down, observed refinery crude intake rose by 1.6 percent or 189,000 bpd from January to 11.709 million bpd. Crude intake was also up in comparison to February last year, by 224,000 bpd.
Euroilstock's figures cover 14 EU member states - all of them with the exception of Sweden.
